summary: The group is 39 runs, almost all on the same San Francisco street extract (createRoads/createAccessScene) or the Chicago commute extract, and nearly every run already writes its spatial inputs through buffers, so most proposals are 'place a node' or 'drag a facility' bindings that need only a pointer-to-nearest-node lookup plus turning a builder.upload of start/facility nodes into a per-frame write. The best pictures are network-service-areas, network-isochrones, network-centrality, edge-bundling and alternative-routes: each shows a clear network output with its inputs. The weakest are the abstract ones with no map: network-statistics (three lone bars), network-cost-table (a dense quarter-width bar strip), the two adjacency-matrix runs (vertical stripes because home-to-work commuting has no community blocks), and network-cost-matrix (an unlabeled heat grid). Several routing pictures never mark their source, sink or origin (network-flow, network-point-routing, network-time-routing, network-line-graph), so the cost field has no visible cause. The facility runs (location-allocation, bounded-facility-allocation, network-facility-optimization, facility-scenario) all draw facilities with a sequential selected/mask ramp while demand uses categorical facility ids that wrap at 8, so demand colour never matches its facility; one shared drawing helper in shared/access.ts would fix all four. Value layers on roads and dots mostly use range 'auto', which hides what costLimit/threshold do to magnitudes. Five runs scrub a Data: knob or rebuild on every step (adjacency-matrix x2, network-analytics-columns, network-statistics, network-structure).

sharedChanges.change: Add a facility drawing helper that colours each candidate by its categorical index (the same id the assignment/nearestFacilities buffers hold), dims unselected or closed ones, and caps the candidate count at 8 so ids never wrap; also make the start/target node lists RunBuffers by default so a facility can be moved per frame.

Add a getEndpointMarkers(positions) helper (pin glyph for origin/source/sink/start) and a getMaskValues look that draws mask 0 muted instead of categorical colour 0, so closed/dropped roads read as absent.
Export a pointer-to-node helper (network.findNearestNode on world coordinates) and a pointer-to-slot-and-fraction helper for directed roads, used by every place/drag binding in the group.

createCommunityGraph builds directed home-to-work links, which concentrate on a few workplace tracts and draw vertical stripes; add a symmetric within-band-weighted variant (or Louvain communities) so grouped order forms diagonal blocks.

frameworkNeeds: pointer position in world coordinates passed to update (values.pointer = [x, y] or null), not only a normalized x scrub
pointer to nearest network node / nearest directed slot with fraction, computed on the CPU from inputs
glyph layer at the pointer: pin, crosshair, ring of a given world radius around a point or around several anchors
highlight of one element on dots, segments and raster layers (value equal to a hovered id drawn bright, others dimmed) without a re-run
chart cursor: vertical rule at pointer x mapped to the chart's x axis, with the series values at that x in the readout
readout of a small GPU scalar (objective, covered demand, flow value, matched count) through a cheap readback after each run
swipe curtain between two layers or two prebuilt variants of a compile-time prop
debounced rebuild for compile-time props bound to the pointer (snap to discrete steps, rebuild after pointer rests)
two-axis pad binding (x and y each to a named parameter) for runs with no spatial handle
chart axis labels and reference lines (expected K(r) = r, zero line) in the chart layer

issues.detail: Directed home-to-work links point at a few workplace tracts, so the matrix is vertical stripes and 'grouped' order shows no blocks.
issues.fix: Use a symmetric tract graph with community structure (createCommunityGraph variant) so blocks appear on the diagonal.
